the dorsal and ventrical language pathways are anatomically parallel and relatively segregated in the subcortical white matter but are strictly overlapped in the terminal cortical regions.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the dorsal and ventrical streams of language are anatomically and functionally integrated, and this integration takes place in a criss-cross fashion at the cortical level, where the terminations of both streams are strictly overlapped, and at the subcortical level, where the fibers of the two streams run in parallel and segregated, but their terminations are connected through the U‐fibres.

the language system, which is usually described as a set of segregated pathways, has a complex anatomical structure that includes parallel and segregated pathways at the subcortical level and a reciprocal anatomical relationship between dorsal and ventrobasal pathways at the cortical level.
